audience: CG owner and Nolan editors comparing native coding capability, not consumers
goal: Demonstrate that a single self-contained HTML/JavaScript composition can produce a perspective device scene, animated metallic typography, controlled camera movement and reflections, with an explicit reusable render clock
palette_source: Owner-supplied CG colours, with lighter tints for lighting and contrast
typography: Arial/Helvetica/system sans for this technical study only; no brand-font or cross-OS font-parity claim
asset_provenance: Original procedural generic laptop and illustrative motion interface; no external assets or actual client screens

beats.job: Metallic screen typography resolves while a close camera reveals device depth
Camera pulls back to a laptop-and-reflection hero with readable title
The screen changes to an illustrative timeline, showing coordinated camera/type/light states
Metallic type returns and the camera settles; clean hierarchy rather than random clip cuts
Resolve to the capability statement, not a fictional commercial claim

sound: SILENT_VISUAL_STUDY; no unreviewed music or reference audio reuse
acceptance: Technical proof only; owner creative acceptance, physical-phone comfort and full reference parity remain separate
